name: James Hawkins

education.notes: Cambridge BA Economics 2007–2010 per Crunchbase / The Org profiles. Y Combinator alum (W20).

keyDecisions: Took a hybrid sales-engineering role at a small UK firm immediately after Cambridge — combined hands-on technical work with commercial reps from the start.
lessons: A 'hybrid' first job (technical + sales/commercial) is rare and high-leverage — it builds both skill stacks in parallel.
Working at smaller UK companies right after Cambridge gave him operating reps that pure-grad-scheme peers didn't get.
careerSteps.notes: Per LinkedIn-derived summaries; overlap with Cambridge final year.

keyDecisions: Founded a new profitable division inside a UK media company — first 'intrapreneur' reps before founding his own company.
Stayed inside a host company rather than spinning out — used the umbrella to validate without raising capital.
lessons: Founding a division inside a company is a legitimate path to founder reps without the financial risk of a venture-backed startup.
Profitable intrapreneurship teaches commercial discipline that VC money often masks.

careerSteps.company: UK B2B SaaS scale-up (and consulting at Arachnys)
keyDecisions: Spent four years selling 7–8 figure enterprise contracts at UK B2B scale-ups — earned the enterprise-sales reps that almost no technical-cofounder has.
Layered a marketing consultancy at Arachnys on the side — extended commercial pattern-recognition across multiple companies.
lessons: Enterprise sales experience is rare and durable — the founder market favours technical CTOs, so a sales-trained CEO is the structurally undervalued half of the pairing.
Working at UK startups that 'just did OK' (rather than rockets) trains you to spot what's missing — the seed of his bigger founding ambition.
careerSteps.notes: Per Sarah Drinkwater Medium fireside chat: 'background of working for UK startups that had just done OK before pursuing bigger ambitions.' Also describes earlier 'developer role (a very bad one)' followed by VP of Sales.

keyDecisions: Co-founded PostHog with technical co-founder Tim Glaser; joined Y Combinator W20 (Jan–Mar 2020).
Pivoted inside YC with four weeks until Demo Day — bet the company on a working open-source product analytics MVP.
Launched on Hacker News immediately after Demo Day — used the open-source artefact + HN to bootstrap distribution.
Sales-trained CEO + engineer CTO co-founder pairing — explicit complementary split unusual in dev-tools where both founders are often engineers.
Built a multiproduct platform (~16–17 products) on top of the analytics wedge — turned single-product PMF into a portfolio.
lessons: Sales-trained CEO + engineering CTO is a structurally undervalued pairing in dev-tools (where both founders are usually engineers).
Open-source artefact + Hacker News launch is still a viable distribution wedge for European dev-tools founders raising US capital.
Pivoting inside YC at the last minute is survivable if your founders are sharp and your tech is shippable in weeks — speed of execution matters more than the original thesis.
Lifestyle is a strategy: building PostHog from a village outside Cambridge rather than relocating to SF — proves UK dev-tools companies can compete globally without geography sacrifice.
careerSteps.notes: PostHog (YC W20) is a single platform for product engineers offering analytics, session recording, feature flags and a broader product suite. Per their own About page, 190,000+ teams use the platform and ~65% of every YC batch uses PostHog. Per the fireside chat, the company reached a mid-tens-of-millions revenue run rate. Publicly disclosed funding includes a Series B (~$15M, 2021, led by GV) and a Series C (~$70M+, 2023, led by Y Combinator alumni-network investors). James and Tim are both Co-CEOs.

outcomes.currentStatus: Co-founder & Co-CEO of PostHog (London / remote-first). Open-source product analytics platform used by 190k+ teams; ~65% of every YC batch uses PostHog. Mid-tens-of-millions revenue run rate per public interviews.

lessons.lesson: Cambridge BA + UK B2B sales + 4 years selling 7–8 figure contracts → YC → founder is the 'sales-trained CEO' template — structurally undervalued vs. the technical-cofounder default.
lessons.source: Synthesised from Sarah Drinkwater fireside chat + Crunchbase profile.

lessons.lesson: Found in your early 30s after a decade of enterprise-sales reps, not at 21 with no commercial reps. Sales experience is the half of founderships that doesn't get taught.
Open-source + Hacker News is still a viable dev-tools wedge — PostHog launched MVP on HN immediately after YC Demo Day in 2020.
Sales CEO + engineer CTO is a structurally undervalued pairing in dev-tools where both founders are usually engineers.
